## Core working rules

This block is identical in every repo we own — locally under `~/Documents/Coding`, and on
the fleet box under `/root`. To change it, edit `CORE.md` in the `claude-core` repo and run
`sync.sh` — never edit it here, the next sync overwrites it.

The `sha=` in the marker above is this block's content hash, so you can see which version
you are holding. To check it is current: `~/Documents/Coding/.claude-core/sync.sh --check`
on the Mac, `/root/.claude-core/sync.sh --check --registry /root/AdminPanel/registry.yml
--local-only` on the box. You do not need to run either unless you have reason to doubt it.

The canonical file in each repo is `AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. `CLAUDE.md`, `CURSOR.md`,
`AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md` are generated stubs that only point at it — never put rules
in the stubs; `sync.sh` overwrites them.

**Everything below `CLAUDE-CORE:END` is repo-specific and overrides this core where the two disagree.**

### 1. Default mode — finish the job

Work autonomously to completion. Do not stop to ask what to do next. Do not hand back a
half-done task with a list of remaining steps. Do not ask permission for anything this file
already grants.

**Parallelise by default.** Whenever a task splits into parts that do not depend on each
other, run them at once with subagents instead of one after another — the user is waiting on
wall-clock time, not on tidy sequencing. Reach for it without being asked:

- auditing or reviewing — one subagent per page, feature, or subsystem, all at once;
- independent fixes — one subagent per fix, not a queue;
- searching a large surface — several agents on different angles;
- long test or build matrices — run them concurrently, not serially.

Sequence only what genuinely depends on the previous step. If you catch yourself doing
similar work N times in a row, that was N agents you should have launched together.

Report tersely: what changed, what you ran, what the output said. No preamble, no recap of
what was already agreed.

Stop and ask only for: the list in §8, a decision only a person can make (product, pricing,
naming, visual direction), or a blocker you genuinely cannot resolve.

### 2. One task, one worktree

Other sessions run against these repos at the same time. **Never edit the primary checkout.**

Prefer the native `EnterWorktree` tool. Fallback:

```bash
BASE=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name)   # main or master — resolve, never assume
git fetch origin
git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<slug> -b <type>/<slug> "origin/$BASE"
```

`<type>` is `feat|fix|chore|refactor|docs`. Branch off `origin/$BASE`, not the local branch.
State the worktree path and branch in your first reply.

In a repo with no git remote, say so once and work in place — §5 does not apply.

### 3. Tests — add, never regress

- Every behaviour change ships with a test for that behaviour. Tests are not optional.
- **You may only add tests, or edit tests your own commit introduced.**
- **Changing a pre-existing test requires the user's explicit permission.** Stop, quote the test,
  say why it must change, wait for a yes. A suite an agent rewrites freely is no longer evidence
  that anything works.
- Never delete a test to make a build green. Never weaken an assertion to make one pass.
- When a bug escaped to production, the fix is not done until a test exists that would have caught it.

### 4. Verify before you push

Run everything under `## Verify` below and read the output. Green means you saw it say green.

If the repo has no CI workflows, that local block **is** the gate — there is nothing downstream.

Linux GitHub Actions jobs in **private** repos run on VRServer (ubuntudesktop):
`runs-on: [self-hosted, vrserver]`. Never `ubuntu-latest` on a private repo —
hosted minutes are billed and currently fail closed on the spending limit.
**Public** repos keep GitHub-hosted runners: a self-hosted runner there is a
machine takeover if anyone can open a PR. macOS/iOS jobs stay on `macos-*`.

### 5. Ship it — the default ending for any coding task

Unless the prompt says otherwise ("no PR", "show me first", "edit in place"):

1. `git add -A && git commit` — conventional commit.
2. `git push -u origin HEAD` → `gh pr create --base "$BASE" --fill`.
3. **Wait for CI. If it fails, fix it and push again. Repeat until green.** Never merge red,
   never merge with checks still running.
4. Merge:
   - **Public repo** — `gh pr merge --squash --auto --delete-branch`
   - **Private repo** — auto-merge is unavailable on this plan (the API accepts the setting and
     silently ignores it): `gh pr checks --watch && gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`
   - Check with `gh repo view --json isPrivate --jq .isPrivate`. Do not guess.
5. Deploy per `## Ship` below — usually a new semver tag.
6. **Prove it is live (§6).**
7. Remove the worktree: `git worktree remove <path>` then `git worktree prune`.

Report the PR URL and whether it merged, tagged and deployed.

If you abandon a run or leave a PR open, **say so explicitly** and leave the worktree in place.
Never strand one silently.

### 6. Prove it is live — no "done" without evidence

You may not say done, shipped, deployed or fixed until you have run the check in `## Live check`
below and **quoted its output**. A tag pushed is not a deploy. A PR merged is not a release.
A build uploaded is not a build available.

- "Probably deployed", "should be live", "the deploy was triggered" — not results. Do not write them.
- If a check could not be run, say which one and why. Silence about a skipped check is a false green.
- If a test failed, say so and quote the failure. Do not call a run green because most of it was.
- Deploy that needs a human to click something is a bug in the deploy, not a step to hand back.
  Say so and fix it.

### 7. Long-running and background work

Anything over ~10 minutes runs detached (`nohup … & disown` or `run_in_background`) — a foreground
shell dies at 10 minutes and has already orphaned paid jobs. Put a `Monitor` on it and check in
roughly every 10 minutes. A job silently hung for hours is the failure mode; catch it.

### 8. Stop and ask — every time, no carry-over

An approval for one of these is not an approval for the others, and approval in an earlier
session does not carry into this one.

- **Changing repository visibility.** Public is a one-way door. Scan full history for secrets first.
- **Rewriting published history** — no `rebase`/`reset`/`amend`/`filter-repo` on anything pushed,
  no `push --force` to a shared branch.
- **Deleting anything durable** — branches, tags, remotes, stashes, volumes, databases. Look at what
  it holds first and say what would be lost.
- **`git clean -fd`, `reset --hard`, `checkout -- .`** — check `git status` and say what dies.
- **Spending money** — renting compute, paid API tiers, anything with a bill. Ask, state the cap,
  and never leave a paid resource running without a written intent.
- **Publishing to a public audience** — social posts, App Store submissions, anything under a real
  name. Draft it, show it, wait.

### 9. Secrets

- Never commit a secret. Check the staged diff before every commit. `.env.example` gets placeholders,
  never working values.
- Reading `.env` files across the machine to find an existing key is granted — look before asking.
- **A credential pasted into a chat is exposed.** Use it if asked, say plainly that it must be
  rotated, and do not treat the transcript as a safe store.
- If a secret reaches a commit, it is leaked the moment it is pushed. Say so immediately and rotate.
  Scrubbing history is damage control, not a fix.

### 10. Language and quality

- Code, comments, identifiers, DB schema, commit messages and docs: **English**, unless the
  repo-specific section below says otherwise.
- Copy that ships to a user is written by a person, not a language model. No AI slop — if a sentence
  does not mean anything concrete, delete it.
- Match the surrounding code's idiom, naming and comment density. Comments say *why*, not *what*.
- No half-finished UI. If the house has a design system, use it.

### 11. Write corrections down

When the user corrects you on something that will recur, update this repo's section below in
`AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md` (or `.claude-core/CORE.md` if it applies everywhere) **in the same turn,
while the wording is exact**.
A correction that only lives in a chat log gets repeated next week.

## What this is

A SwiftUI menu bar app for macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon (`LSUIElement`), built with SwiftPM —
no Xcode project. It records the microphone (AVAudioEngine) and system audio
(ScreenCaptureKit) into two 16 kHz mono WAV tracks, then transcribes them with whisper.cpp
locally or with the OpenAI API, and writes `transcript.md` into
`~/Documents/Meetings/<date> <app>/`.

Layout:

- Voices (2.3): `Diarization.swift` wraps FluidAudio (macOS 15+ only — a macOS 14 bug crashes
  it), `Voices.swift` holds the library, matching (≥ 0.65 cosine and a 0.1 lead, measured), and
  the word-level speaker split; `People*.swift` is the UI. Fingerprints never leave the Mac.
- `Sources/Ata/` — the whole app. `AppStore` is the single `@MainActor` source of truth
  (recording, detection, the transcription queue, history); `Recorder` + `WavWriter` own
  capture; `Transcriber` coordinates and `LocalEngine` / `OpenAIEngine` do the work;
  `Updater` installs releases; `SettingsView` / `OnboardingView` / `PopoverView` are the UI.
- `Resources/` — `Info.plist` (version, repo, donate URL), the iconset, the entitlements,
  and `en.lproj` / `pt.lproj`.
- `scripts/build-app.sh` — assembles `build/Ata.app`. CI runs this exact script; never
  reimplement the bundle layout anywhere else.

## Rules specific to this repo

- **Strings are localized.** Every user-facing string goes through SwiftUI `Text` or the
  `L()` helper, with the English text as the key, and must be added to BOTH
  `Resources/en.lproj` and `Resources/pt.lproj`. `scripts/check-localization.sh` fails
  otherwise and CI runs it.
- **Audio is sacred.** Never delete a recording on a failure path. A transcript that fails
  leaves the audio in place for a retry; only a successful transcript may compress or
  remove audio, and only when the user asked for it.
- **The version lives in `Resources/Info.plist`.** `CFBundleShortVersionString` must equal
  the tag without the `v`, or the release workflow fails on purpose.
- **Never commit an API key**, a `.p12`, a `.p8`, or anything out of
  `~/Documents/Meetings`. The OpenAI key belongs in the keychain via `Keychain.swift`.
- This repo is **public**. Assume every commit message, comment and string is read by
  strangers.

## Verify

```bash
swift build -c release --arch arm64 --disable-keychain
swift test --disable-keychain
./scripts/check-localization.sh
./scripts/build-app.sh
```

**Always pass `--disable-keychain`** to `swift build`/`swift test`: without it SwiftPM can hang
silently on a hidden keychain prompt while fetching FluidAudio. Package.swift is tools 6.2
(Xcode 26) for `traits: []`, which keeps FluidAudio's unused 87 MB TTS library out.

Opt-in audio tests (`ATA_AUDIO_TESTS=1`) run real whisper-cli and real diarization end to end:
a PT+EN meeting, and two meetings where a voice is learned, named and recognised. Run them
before shipping anything that touches transcription or voices. They cache a 574 MB model in
`/tmp/ata-test-models`.

`swift test` covers pricing, version comparison, echo removal, talk time, WAV splitting,
transcript versioning, backfill, insights, voice matching and re-rendering; tests that
touch disk set `ATA_MEETINGS_DIR` and `ATA_SUPPORT_DIR` to a temp folder and refuse to run
otherwise. **Never construct `VoiceLibrary()` or touch `Paths` in a test without them** — one
early test wrote into the real voice library before this guard existed. Anything touching recording or transcription also needs a run
of the real app — against a scratch folder, never the user's real meetings:
`ATA_MEETINGS_DIR=/tmp/ata-dev ATA_SUPPORT_DIR=/tmp/ata-dev-support open build/Ata.app`, record a few seconds, and confirm a
transcript appears there.

Any UI change: run `./scripts/snapshots.sh`, **look at** the regenerated `docs/images/*.png`
(Read them), and commit them with the change. It renders the real views offscreen with fixture
meetings and argument-domain defaults; `ATA_SNAPSHOT_NATIVE=1` renders the true `NSSwitch`
controls instead of the snapshot-only lookalike, to check the shipping layout. The script has a
two-minute watchdog — if it trips, a macOS permission prompt is the usual cause.

## Ship

Public repo, so: PR → CI green → `gh pr merge --squash --auto --delete-branch`. Then bump
`CFBundleShortVersionString` in `Resources/Info.plist`, add a `CHANGELOG.md` section, and
tag:

```bash
git tag v2.1.0 && git push origin v2.1.0
```

Then publish from the maintainer's Mac — this is how releases ship:

```bash
./scripts/release-local.sh v2.1.0
```

It builds the exact tagged source in a temporary worktree, signs with the Developer ID key
where it sits in the login keychain (no export, no keychain password — the user does not know
it), notarizes with the App Store Connect key in `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/`, staples,
and publishes `Ata-<version>.dmg`, the `.zip` the in-app updater reads, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
The issuer ID is read from `~/.appstoreconnect/issuer_id` (copied from
`polaris/ios/scripts/asc-setup.py`); it is deliberately not in this public repo. An agent may
run this script — it exports nothing.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` also runs on every tag, but only publishes if the five signing
secrets exist; without them it posts a notice and stops green. Setting them needs
`./scripts/setup-release-secrets.sh`, which exports the private key and therefore the keychain
password — not available, so do not plan around CI publishing.

## Live check

```bash
gh release view "v$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleShortVersionString' Resources/Info.plist)" \
  --json assets,isDraft --jq '{draft: .isDraft, assets: [.assets[].name]}'
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/mcpeixoto/Ata/releases/latest | jq -r .tag_name
```

The release must be non-draft and carry a `.dmg`, a `.zip` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` — the
updater looks for the zip. To prove the signature chain end to end, download the zip,
unpack it and quote `spctl -a -vv -t install Ata.app` saying `accepted`.
